findings.reason: a coordinator reading the followups as the build queue would dispatch a completed investigation and would find no pointer to §31, so the plan's forward wiring must be repaired (resolve `f-ahdwift-s25b`, add the §31 followup) before it is built.
findings.text: the open followup `f-ahdwift-s25b` still commands `/reckon-build a-held-dispatch-waits-its-fair-turn §25` while the identical document declares §25 `done` (section tag line 165) and its own comment `c-close-s25` records it closed; §31, the section §25's Deliverable promised to file ("That change is filed as a new section"), has no followup naming it

findings.reason: the cause §31 names (the allowance read at different instants) is the one the evidence supports, and the inflated count in the Why does not change the mechanism or the done-when a builder implements.
findings.text: §31's Why says the pass "held the request silently, 38,333 times", but the cited report attributes 38,333 to the service's own lifetime pass count (`{"ok": true, "passes": 38333}` printed over its ~49-hour life, report.md §4), while the request waited ~3.8 h; the report never claims 38,333 holds for this request, and the same misreading is repeated in the s25 close comment (line 585)

rubric_items.done_when: pass — §31's done-when is measurable and carries a negative control that removes the new check and fails the first case, and each of its three cases is falsifiable.
